cards.text: John has been writing down a vision on the island of Patmos (Revelation 1:9), and he's just finished the messages to the seven churches (Revelation 2-3). Now he looks and sees a door standing open in heaven. The voice he heard before, the one like a trumpet, calls out, “Come up here,” and promises to show him something.

cards.question: The trumpet-like voice calls John up through the open door in heaven. What does it promise to show him?

answers.text: What must happen after these things
The day and hour of the end
Where the garden of Eden stood

cards.text: At once John is in the Spirit, and he sees a throne standing in heaven with someone seated on it. No waiting room, no take-a-number ticket, no hold music, friend, just straight to the THRONE.
The One seated there looks like jasper and carnelian. Me on my best day? I look like a stamper somebody dropped in the flour bin.

cards.question: Something that gleams like an emerald circles the throne John is seeing. What is it?

cards.text: And this throne has company. Surrounding it are twenty-four other thrones, and every one of them is taken.

cards.question: Who is sitting on the twenty-four thrones around the throne?
The elders on the twenty-four thrones are dressed in white, with golden crowns on their heads.

cards.text: From the throne come flashes of lightning, rumblings and peals of thunder. Friend, my oven timer dings and I hop three feet in the air, gold base and all, so THUNDER would have me hiding under a mixing bowl.

cards.question: Before the throne, seven torches of fire are burning. What does John say they are?

cards.text: Before the throne is something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal. Around the throne are four living creatures covered with eyes in front and back, and here I am with two eyes and I STILL can't find my rolling pin.

cards.question: Each living creature looks different. The second is like a calf, the third has a face like a man and the fourth is like an eagle in flight. The first one is like a ___.

cards.text: Each of the four living creatures has six wings and is covered with eyes all around and within. And they have something to say about God.

cards.question: The four living creatures stop praising God at night so they can rest.

cards.text: Day and night they never stop saying: “Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come!” No snooze button, no lunch break, NOTHING, and I hit snooze twice before my ovens even warm up.

cards.question: The living creatures call the Lord God Almighty the One who was and is and is to come. What does that tell you about Him?

answers.text: He has always been and always will be
He ruled long ago but has stepped away
He is only now beginning to reign

cards.text: Whenever the living creatures give glory, honor and thanks to the One seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever, the twenty-four elders fall down and worship Him. Every single time.

cards.question: As the twenty-four elders fall down and worship, what do they do with their golden crowns?

answers.text: Hand them to the living creatures

cards.question: The elders tell the Lord God that He is worthy to receive glory and honor and power. What reason do they give?

answers.text: He opened a door in heaven

cards.text: Then John sees a scroll in the right hand of the One seated on the throne. It has writing on both sides and seven seals on it, and friend, I can't open ONE cookie box without a fight.
A mighty angel calls out in a loud voice: “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?”

cards.question: The mighty angel asks who is worthy to open the scroll. Who in heaven or on earth or under the earth is able to do it?
No one is found worthy to open the scroll or even look inside it. How does John react?

answers.text: He tries to open it himself
He falls on his face in fear

cards.text: Friend, I cried in that junk drawer over a lot less than a sealed scroll, so I get it. But then one of the elders says to John, “Do not weep!” and tells him someone has triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals.

cards.question: The elder tells John someone has triumphed to open the scroll. What does the elder call Him?

answers.text: The Lion of the tribe of Judah
The Star that comes out of Jacob
The Prophet raised up like Moses

cards.question: The elder just announced the Lion of the tribe of Judah. But what does John see standing in the center of the throne?

answers.text: A Lamb that appeared to have been slain
A lion wearing a golden crown
A mighty angel holding a sword

cards.text: Let that sit a second, friend. The elder says Lion, John looks, and there stands a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, with seven horns and seven eyes.

cards.question: The Lamb has seven horns and seven eyes. What does John say they represent?

cards.text: Remember, no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth could open that scroll or even look inside it. Now the Lamb comes to the One seated on the throne.

cards.question: The Lamb waits for the mighty angel to hand Him the scroll.

cards.text: When He takes the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fall down before the Lamb. Each one has a harp, and they're holding golden bowls full of incense.

cards.question: The living creatures and the elders hold golden bowls full of incense before the Lamb. What does John say the incense is?

cards.text: Think about it, friend: I spent years next to receipts nobody needed, and up there the prayers of the saints are held in golden bowls. Then they sing a new song to the Lamb.

cards.question: In their new song, why do they say the Lamb is worthy to take the scroll and open its seals?

answers.text: He was slain and purchased people for God
He is the oldest one in all of heaven
The mighty angel chose Him for the job

cards.question: By His blood the Lamb purchased people for God. Where are those people from?

answers.text: Every tribe and tongue and nation

cards.text: The song goes on: He made them a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will reign upon the earth. Me? I got moved from a junk drawer to a cookie planet and I STILL haven't calmed down.

Then John hears the voices of many angels encircling the throne, along with the living creatures and the elders, and their number is myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands. In a loud voice they say: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing!”

cards.question: Earlier, no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth could open the scroll. Now who joins in praising the One on the throne and the Lamb?

cards.text: Every creature gives praise and honor and glory and power forever and ever to Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb, the four living creatures say, “Amen,” and the elders fall down and worship. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, but keep your apron on, because this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: John shows up for the first time in this passage, but the card never says who he is. It only says he has been writing down a vision on Patmos. A simple identifier with its reference is needed, such as His servant John (Revelation 1:1).

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says twenty-four thrones, and only the right answer carries the number twenty-four. The wrong answers say seven and twelve. The right answer stands out by matching the number, so the baker gets it without thinking about the scene.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess a detail of the vision (lion, bear or leopard) with nothing to reason from. It is the same pattern as the bad Psalm 23 example about guessing what anoints David's head. It tests wording and detail the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: **Ask about the movement and the meaning:** what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards are pure discovery questions about vision details: card 2 (what the voice promises), card 5 (rainbow), card 7 (elders), card 8 (white robes and gold crowns), card 10 (seven spirits), card 12 (lion), card 14 (no setup about day and night) and card 18 (casting crowns). Only cards 16 and 19 can be reasoned out. That is more than a few discovery questions.

rule.text: **A few discovery questions are fine.** Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card makes up a new backstory fact: that Papa Dorin cried in the junk drawer. The backstory says he went quiet and stopped joking. It never says he cried. Made-up moments in jokes are allowed around his bakery, not as new facts about the drawer years.

rule.text: **His own world isn't Bible fact.** His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The elder calls Him both the Lion of the tribe of Judah and the Root of David (Revelation 5:5). No card ever mentions the Root of David, so the baker leaves Prep without an important title from the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The setup says "The elder just announced the Lion… But what does John see". The word But tells the baker it isn't a lion, which rules out the wrong answer "A lion wearing a golden crown." The right answer is also noticeably longer than the other two.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The Lamb shows up for the first time, and no card ever says who He is. Papa Dorin knows the Lamb is Jesus, God's Son (John 1:29), and facts from outside the passage are allowed with their reference. Without this, the baker may not connect the Lamb to Jesus, or to the Marriage Supper of the Lamb.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card opens by recapping Revelation 5:3 ("Remember, no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth could open that scroll"). Card 3 already asked about this and card 4 restated it. Only the last half-sentence moves the passage forward.

Card 18 already showed the angels praising, and the question asks who "joins in". That rules out "Only the many angels". The two wrong answers both start with Only, while the right answer echoes the setup's heaven, earth and under-the-earth contrast, so it stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card packs several beats into one long comma-joined sentence: every creature's praise, the living creatures' Amen and the elders falling down to worship. The story-continues line comes after that. This goes over the two-beat limit.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
